questions.question: At stops, a driver should:

options.text: Warn passengers about hazards as they exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn passengers about hazards as they exit.
questions.explanation: At bus stops, warn passengers about potential hazards. Tell them to watch their step when exiting the bus, especially when using lowered stairways.

questions.question: On surfaces with poor traction, a driver should accelerate slowly to:

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
Keep from losing control of the vehicle.
Not go faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep from losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly in poor-traction conditions, such as rain or snow. This prevents loss of control.

questions.question: When re-entering traffic after a bus stop, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will let you merge into traffic.
Wait for a large enough gap to merge into traffic.
Have a passenger stop traffic so you can merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large enough gap to merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: After a bus stop, wait for a gap in traffic that is large enough for your vehicle to accelerate and merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer:

options.text: You should not back up in a straight line.
You should not correct drift until you are far off course.
You should pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.
questions.explanation: Pull forward to reposition your vehicle whenever needed when backing. Correct drift immediately by steering in the direction of the drift.

questions.question: Front tire tread depth should be at least ____ in every major groove.
questions.correctAnswerText: 4/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Front tires must have a tread depth of 4/32 of an inch in every major groove. Other tires need 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: On any uphill grade, gravity will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow your vehicle down.
questions.explanation: Gravity slows your vehicle on uphill grades. You may need to shift to a lower gear to climb a steep grade.

questions.question: Bridges usually:
questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces. Be extra careful on bridges when temperatures are near freezing.

questions.question: Bridges usually freeze:

options.text: Only when temperatures drop far below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces. Drive carefully on bridges when temperatures are close to freezing.

questions.question: A distracted driver usually:

options.text: Follows the rules of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has slower perception of hazards.
questions.explanation: Distracted drivers notice hazards more slowly than focused drivers. Sometimes they don't notice hazards at all.

questions.question: After picking up passengers at a stop, a driver should:

options.text: Give passengers time to sit or brace themselves before driving.
Honk the horn and re-enter traffic.
Begin driving as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give passengers time to sit or brace themselves before driving.
questions.explanation: Start and stop smoothly to prevent passenger injury. After passengers board, let them sit or brace themselves before you begin driving.

questions.question: If you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test, what happens?

options.text: You lose extra points on your final score.
You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If you are driving a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly causes automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay alert while driving?

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before you start driving.
Drive with another person who can take turns driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with another person who can take turns driving.
questions.explanation: Having a second driver reduces the risk that either driver will become tired. You can also stay alert by avoiding heavy meals and keeping the cab cool.

questions.question: What happens to brakes as a vehicle gets heavier?
questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes must work harder.
questions.explanation: Heavier vehicles require more braking power to stop completely.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain what you inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid a hazard?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
You may need to swerve out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may need to swerve out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you do not have enough space to stop, swerving may be your safest option.

questions.question: When the examiner asks you to change lanes during the driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes quickly, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When asked to change lanes during the on-road driving test, check your mirrors and use proper signals before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth required for rear tires?
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch.
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Rear tires and other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch of tread depth. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks during the driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out and check for a train.
Do not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver confronts you?

options.text: Make eye contact to communicate with them.
Do not move out of their path.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore their gestures.
questions.explanation: If confronted by an aggressive driver, get out of their way if possible. Do not make eye contact, as this could provoke them. Do not respond to their actions.

questions.question: While passengers are on a bus, what are refueling in an enclosed space, allowing the bus to be towed, and talking with passengers considered to be?
questions.correctAnswerText: Prohibited practices.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must not talk with passengers, refuel a bus inside a building, or tow or push a disabled bus with passengers aboard. These are all prohibited practices.
